"PEDAL LIFE – ISOMETRIC BICYCLE DELIVERY LIFE SIMULATOR

Create a 2D isometric life simulation game focused on bicycle deliveries, survival needs, personal finances, and daily life management.

IMPORTANT: All in-game text, menus, dialogues, missions, interface elements, notifications, and item descriptions must be in Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR).

1. GAME STYLE AND WORLD

- 2D isometric perspective.
- Detailed and colorful urban environment.
- Explore neighborhoods, residential streets, commercial areas, restaurants, supermarkets, parks, and other locations.
- Smooth character movement in eight directions.
- Bicycle riding animations.
- Dynamic day and night cycle.
- Weather system, including sunny days and rain.
- Interactive buildings and objects.
- Immersive urban atmosphere.

2. STARTING STORY

The player starts with very little money and a borrowed bicycle.

The main character wants to earn money working as a bicycle delivery courier and improve their quality of life.

The first major objective is to save enough money to purchase their first BMX bicycle.

The player must work hard, manage their daily needs, and make financial decisions.

3. DELIVERY JOB SYSTEM

Create a functional delivery system.

- Restaurants, grocery stores, and local businesses offer delivery orders.
- Each order has a pickup location and a delivery destination.
- Every delivery has a deadline based on distance and estimated travel time.
- Deliveries completed on time provide full payment.
- Late deliveries reduce payment and customer ratings.
- Fast and successful deliveries can generate tips.
- The player can accept or reject available orders.
- Different orders offer different rewards.
- The player must physically travel to the business, collect the order, and deliver it to the customer.

Create a working delivery interface showing destination, deadline, payment, and distance.

4. CHARACTER SURVIVAL SYSTEM

The player has four important needs:

HUNGER:

- Hunger decreases over time.
- The player must purchase or prepare food.
- Low hunger reduces stamina and performance.

THIRST:

- Thirst decreases over time, especially during physical activity.
- The player must drink water or other beverages.
- Dehydration negatively affects performance.

SLEEP:

- The character becomes tired after staying awake for too long.
- Low sleep reduces movement speed and stamina.
- The player must return home to sleep.

ENERGY:

- Cycling and physical activities consume energy.
- Rest and sleep restore energy.
- Low energy makes deliveries more difficult.

All needs must be represented by functional status bars.

5. HOME AND PERSONAL LIFE

The player owns a small home that serves as their safe place and resting area.

Inside the house, the player can:

- Sleep and advance the game clock.
- Eat food.
- Drink water.
- Check their money.
- Manage their inventory.
- Interact with their pet dog.

The home must be enterable and explorable.

6. PET DOG SYSTEM

The player owns a dog that is an important part of their life.

The dog has its own needs:

- Hunger.
- Thirst.
- Attention.

The player must feed the dog, provide water, and interact with it.

The dog should have animations, movement, and reactions to the player's presence.

The dog should follow the player inside the house and behave like a real companion.

Pet care must be part of the daily gameplay routine.

7. BICYCLE PROGRESSION AND CUSTOMIZATION

The player begins with a borrowed bicycle.

Allow the player to save money and purchase different bicycles:

- Basic BMX.
- Upgraded BMX.
- Urban bicycle.
- Professional delivery bicycle.

Each bicycle must have different attributes:

- Maximum speed.
- Acceleration.
- Durability.
- Pedaling efficiency.

Allow bicycle upgrades and visual customization.

The player's first BMX purchase should feel like a meaningful achievement.

8. FINANCIAL SYSTEM

Create a functional economy.

The player earns money through completed deliveries.

Money can be spent on:

- Food.
- Drinks (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
